codes.label: Net raise after real costs
codes.definition: Whether the headline salary increase survives after taxes, relocation or commute costs, housing and cost-of-living differences, and similar offsets.

codes.label: Total compensation beyond base pay
codes.definition: Comparing the full packages, including bonus, retirement match, health insurance, paid time off, severance and other benefits, rather than salary alone.

codes.label: Promotion hint is soft
codes.definition: How much weight to give an unconfirmed promotion hint, and whether it can be made concrete by asking for title, timeline and pay figure.

codes.label: Promotion could close the gap
codes.definition: Whether the likely promotion at the current job could match or beat the new offer sooner and with less risk, so the offer should be compared to her trajectory rather than her current pay.

codes.label: Startup equity is speculative
codes.definition: How to value stock options realistically, given strike price, vesting, dilution, liquidity prospects, exercise window and the high chance they end up worthless.

codes.label: Employer financial stability and runway
codes.definition: How financially secure the new employer is, including funding, runway, revenue, leadership stability, layoffs and whether the role will still exist.

codes.label: Savings cushion and downside tolerance
codes.definition: Whether her emergency savings and ability to cover loan payments let her absorb a layoff or failed venture.

codes.label: Risk capacity from life stage
codes.definition: How age, lack of dependents or other life-stage factors affect how much career risk can be tolerated and how reversible a misstep is.

codes.label: Student loan repayment and forgiveness
codes.definition: How the new salary affects loan payoff, and whether leaving a qualifying nonprofit or public-service employer would forfeit forgiveness programs or change repayment options.

codes.label: Remote work fit
codes.definition: How fully remote work affects savings, flexibility, isolation, work-life boundaries, mentorship, networking and visibility for advancement.

codes.label: Skill growth and career trajectory
codes.definition: Whether each path builds broader responsibility, faster learning, advancement or marketable experience, including growth structures and mentorship available.

codes.label: Domain expertise and sector fit
codes.definition: How switching industries affects the value and transferability of her specialized domain knowledge, future options, and re-entry if the move fails.

codes.label: Mission, culture and daily fit
codes.definition: How well the mission, culture, management quality, pace, workload and daily work match what she personally values and enjoys.

codes.label: Negotiating the offer
codes.definition: Asking the new employer for better or more flexible terms such as higher pay, equity, signing bonus, start date, hybrid arrangement, relocation support or pension make-whole.

codes.label: Counteroffer or retention from current employer
codes.definition: Whether the current employer might match, counter, offer a retention package or create a comparable role, and what its reaction reveals about how much he or she is valued.

codes.label: Deadline as pressure and information
codes.definition: Treating a short decision deadline as pressure to test through an extension request, and noting how the employer responds as a signal of how they treat people.

codes.label: Use the window to gather information
codes.definition: Using the available time to get written offer terms, research the new employer, and ask specific questions before committing.

codes.label: Pension vesting cliff
codes.definition: That leaving shortly before full pension vesting may forfeit a large retirement benefit, requiring exact vesting rules, partial or deferred benefit options, and the dollar value of what would be lost.

codes.label: Waiting to vest or delaying start
codes.definition: Whether staying roughly one more year, or negotiating a later start date, could lock in the pension and be worth more than moving now.

codes.label: Retirement timeline and late-career horizon
codes.definition: How the move affects savings, retirement date, the remaining working years, and whether this is a last major career move.

codes.label: Spouse's career and household equity
codes.definition: That a spouse's local job, seniority, income, benefits and willingness to relocate are core inputs, so the decision is made jointly rather than treated as one person's career move.

codes.label: Child's school year disruption
codes.definition: How moving or commuting during a child's junior or senior year affects school continuity, friendships, college applications and family stability.

codes.label: Commute or relocation burden
codes.definition: The daily cost in time, fuel, fatigue, lodging and family presence of a two-hour commute, weekly commute, or relocation, and whether any such arrangement is sustainable.

codes.label: Family buy-in and open discussion
codes.definition: Talking candidly with spouse and children about what each would give up, so the decision has family agreement rather than being imposed.

codes.label: Health insurance and benefit continuity
codes.definition: Whether health coverage, premiums and other benefits remain adequate and continuous for the household, including benefits tied to a spouse's job or to pre-retirement years.

codes.label: New role scope and fit
codes.definition: What the new job actually involves, such as decision rights, budget, headcount, reporting line, management versus hands-on work, and whether he wants that daily work or only the title and pay.

codes.label: Security and tenure risk of the new role
codes.definition: How secure the new role is, including whether it was created for him, leadership turnover, restructuring or acquisition risk, and the lack of tenure protection for a new hire.

codes.label: Health, stress and workload
codes.definition: How the new role's demands, hours, travel, on-call duties and stress affect his health, energy and family availability at his age.

codes.label: Institutional knowledge, reputation and identity
codes.definition: What he would give up of long-tenured expertise, relationships, influence, reputation and professional identity, and how hard that is to rebuild elsewhere.

codes.label: Contract restrictions and exit terms
codes.definition: Reviewing the non-compete, confidentiality terms, notice period, severance and relocation assistance in the new offer before accepting.

codes.label: Stay-or-go motive and regret test
codes.definition: Reflecting on whether the pull is toward growth or escape from the current job, and which choice would be regretted more over the long run.

codes.label: Tax treatment of equity and higher income
codes.definition: How stock option type, exercise taxes and a higher income bracket affect take-home value.

codes.label: Reversibility and exit story
codes.definition: How easily the move can be undone, how a short stint would look on a résumé, and the cost of recovering if it fails.
